chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one with stomach trouble, and the broken (of body parts), Tawaaf would be performed on their behalf, and the rocks would be pelted on their behalf.

key_terms.الْكَسِيرُ: One with broken bones or limbs
key_terms.الْمَبْطُونُ: One suffering from stomach trouble or illness

ai.seo_question: How can a sick person perform Tawaaf and stoning during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'Tawaaf al-badal' (substitute circumambulation) and 'Ramy al-Jamarat' for those incapacitated by illness or injury, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease in worship. It highlights the permissibility of delegation in core Hajj rituals when physical exertion becomes a hardship, a principle rooted in the Quranic maxim of 'no burden beyond capacity.'
